_comment: BREACHPOINT - the INPUT PROFILE (Tools/gen_input/, ticket BP01 step 3b).
This file is the source of truth for the eleven UInputAction assets, the DA_InputConfig
rows, and the IMC_Default key bindings. Content/Input/*.uasset is its PROJECTION.
CLAUDE.md law 7: input assets are generated by committed scripts, never hand-placed - so
a rebind is an edit HERE plus a re-run, never a drag in the editor.
WHAT THIS FILE MAY AND MAY NOT DECIDE.
It chooses among legal values; it cannot legalise an illegal one. The contract constants
- eleven actions, the exact tag lists, Axis2D for Move/Look, and the ability TRIGGER
CONTRACT (default/empty or Down; never Pressed) - are constants in input_plan.py and are
deliberately NOT readable from here. A gate a data file can weaken is not a gate (the same
rule Tools/blockout/blockout_profile.json states for the BP07 kickoff thresholds).
These are NOT law-3 gameplay tuning numbers: nothing here is read at runtime. They are
authoring constants for an editor-time generator. The gameplay-facing half of input is the
InputTag, and the tag lists below are transcribed from BREACHPOINT-ARCHITECTURE.md 3.2 and
Source/Breachpoint/Core/BRGameplayTags.h - nothing here is invented.
generator_owns_mappings=false means: the generator NEVER touches this action's key
bindings in IMC_Default. The three template actions (Move/Look/Jump) keep the template's
mappings, modifiers and swizzles exactly as authored - re-running this script cannot
disturb them. Only the eight new actions are generator-owned.
NOT COVERED, on purpose (extension points, each a data edit plus a re-run):
- gamepad bindings: none. The packet's defaults are keyboard/mouse; inventing a pad
layout is a design call nobody made. Add keys here when someone makes it.
- per-mapping modifiers/triggers: the eight new mappings are plain digital keys and need
none. build_input.py REFUSES a non-empty modifiers list rather than silently dropping
it, so this is a known limit, not a silent one.
- IA_MouseLook: a UE template asset that is not one of the eleven and is referenced by
IMC_MouseLook, not by IMC_Default. It is listed in unmanaged_actions purely so a reader
can see it was considered and left alone, not forgotten.

unmanaged_actions.why: UE First-Person template asset, consumed by IMC_MouseLook. Not one of the eleven; not in DA_InputConfig; never written or read by this generator.

actions.name: IA_Move
actions.description: Ground movement, 2D. Template asset - value type and triggers are asserted, mappings are left to the template.

actions.name: IA_Look
actions.description: Camera look, 2D. Template asset - mappings (mouse XY + pad stick, with the template's negate/swizzle modifiers) are left alone.

actions.name: IA_Jump
actions.description: Jump. Template asset - Space Bar and pad face button stay as the template authored them.

actions.name: IA_Crouch
actions.description: Crouch. Native, not an ability (ABRCharacter::Crouch/UnCrouch). Hold-to-crouch: the empty trigger set gives Started on press and Completed on release, which is what a hold needs.

actions.name: IA_Sprint
actions.description: Sprint. BRGA_Sprint is the WhileHeld pattern-prover (ARCHITECTURE 3.3) - a Pressed trigger here would end the ability one frame after the press. THE reason the trigger contract exists.

actions.name: IA_Fire
actions.description: Primary fire. Held fire needs a real release edge; see the trigger contract.

actions.name: IA_Swap
actions.description: Weapon swap. Mouse-wheel swap is the obvious alternative binding - add MouseScrollUp/MouseScrollDown to this keys list; it needs no code change.

actions.name: IA_Melee
actions.description: Melee. V rather than F: F is the traditional 'use/interact' slot and BP-later may want it.

actions.name: IA_Grapple
actions.description: Grapple (BP06). Two keys because the grapple is the movement identity verb and thumb-vs-finger preference splits hard; both are digital, neither collides.
